method: Static code-diff analysis in two steps. (1) Per-opcode semantic comparison of each candidate's run() against spec.md for PUSH, ADD, DUP, SWAP, POP including underflow/empty-stack and halting behavior. Deltas found: Candidate A — POP on an empty stack returns "ERROR", whereas the spec says the stack stays empty and the program continues (trigger condition: POP executed with stack depth 0); all other A opcodes match the spec. Candidate B — zero deltas: every opcode, including POP-on-empty (continue) and SWAP/ADD/DUP underflow (immediate "ERROR" halt), matches the spec exactly, so B conforms on all inputs by construction. Candidate C — SWAP with fewer than two values is a silent no-op and the program continues, whereas the spec halts immediately with "ERROR" (trigger condition: SWAP executed with stack depth < 2); all other C opcodes match the spec. (2) First-trigger scan: for A and C, programs in programs.json were scanned in order, tracking only the stack depth at each instruction under the spec's semantics, to find the first program reaching a delta's trigger. A: program 0 (PUSH 3; PUSH 4; ADD — depths 1,2,1) never executes POP on an empty stack; program 1 (PUSH 1; POP; POP; PUSH 9) reaches the second POP at depth 0 — trigger hit. Confirmed difference on program 1 only: spec continues past the empty-stack POP and ends with 9 on top (result 9), while A returns "ERROR"; results differ, so A diverges at index 1. C: programs 0, 1, and 2 contain no SWAP instruction, so C's trigger cannot fire; program 3 (PUSH 5; SWAP; PUSH 1) executes SWAP at depth 1 — trigger hit. Confirmed difference on program 3 only: spec halts immediately with "ERROR", while C no-ops the SWAP, continues, pushes 1, and returns 1; results differ, so C diverges at index 3. No full side-by-side trace simulation of every program against every candidate was performed; per-program computation was used only for the depth-based trigger scan and to confirm the result difference at each identified first-trigger program.
